"Let's build a small Markdown-to-HTML converter in Python, step by step. Start with the basics. Create a package `mdlite` (a directory `mdlite/` with `__init__.py`) exposing `to_html(text: str) -> str`: - A blank line (empty or only whitespace) separates blocks. - A line starting with 1 to 6 `#` followed by a space is a heading: `## Some title` becomes `

Some title

`. A heading line is always a block of its own, even without blank lines around it. `#Title` (no space) and 7 or more `#` are ordinary text. - Any other run of consecutive non-blank lines is a paragraph: each line is stripped and the lines are joined with a single space, `

Hello world

`. - Escape `&`, `<` and `>` in text as `&`, `<` and `>`. - The output is the block elements joined with `\n`, with no trailing newline. Empty input gives `\"\"`. Example: `\"# Title\nSome\ntext\n\nMore\"` gives `\"

Title

\n

Some text

\n

More

\"`. Add pytest tests in `tests/`. The tests run with `python -m pytest`. "

input.oldString:
def to_html(text: str) -> str:
    """Convert a Markdown string to HTML.

    Blank lines separate blocks. A heading is always a block of its own, even
    when it is not surrounded by blank lines. Any other run of consecutive
    non-blank lines becomes one paragraph whose lines are stripped and joined
    with a single space. Block elements are joined with ``\\n`` and there is no
    trailing newline. Empty (or whitespace-only) input yields ``""``.
    """
    blocks: list[str] = []
    paragraph: list[str] = []

    for line in text.split("\n"):
        if _is_blank(line):
            _flush_paragraph(paragraph, blocks)
            continue

        heading = _HEADING_RE.match(line)
        if heading is not None:
            # A heading ends whatever paragraph is open and stands alone.
            level = len(heading.group(1))
            title = heading.group(2).strip()
            blocks.append(f"<h{level}>{_render_inline(title)}</h{level}>")
        else:
            paragraph.append(line)

    _flush_paragraph(paragraph, blocks)
    return "\n".join(blocks)

def to_html(text: str) -> str:
    """Convert a Markdown string to HTML.

    Blank lines separate blocks. The recognised block kinds are ATX
    headings (always a block of their own, even without surrounding blank
    lines), fenced code blocks (opened by a line starting with triple
    backticks, optionally followed by a language, and closed by the next
    line that is exactly triple backticks), unordered lists (consecutive
    lines starting with ``- `` or ``* ``), ordered lists (consecutive lines
    starting with a number, a dot and a space, as in ``1. `` or ``10. ``),
    and paragraphs (any other run of consecutive non-blank lines, whose
    lines are stripped and joined with a single space).

    A paragraph or list ends at a blank line or at the first line that
    starts a block of another kind, which begins the next block. Lines
    inside a code block are emitted verbatim (escaped, unformatted,
    indentation kept); blank lines do not end the block, and an unclosed
    fence runs to the end of the input. Block elements are joined with
    ``\\n`` and there is no trailing newline. Empty (or whitespace-only)
    input yields ``""``.
    """
    blocks: list[str] = []
    lines = text.split("\n")
    n = len(lines)
    i = 0
    while i < n:
        line = lines[i]
        if _is_blank(line):
            i += 1
            continue
        if line.startswith(_FENCE):
            # Fenced code block: consume to the next exact fence or EOF.
            language = line[len(_FENCE):].strip()
            body: list[str] = []
            i += 1
            while i < n and lines[i] != _FENCE:
                body.append(lines[i])
                i += 1
            i += 1
            blocks.append(_render_code_block(language, body))
            continue
        heading = _HEADING_RE.match(line)
        if heading is not None:
            # A heading stands alone and ends whatever block was open.
            level = len(heading.group(1))
            title = heading.group(2).strip()
            blocks.append(f"<h{level}>{_render_inline(title)}</h{level}>")
            i += 1
            continue
        item = _ULIST_RE.match(line)
        if item is None:
            item = _OLIST_RE.match(line)
        if item is not None:
            # Consecutive items of the same kind form one list; the first
            # item of the other kind starts the next block.
            items, i = _collect_items(lines, i, item.re)
            tag = "ul" if item.re is _ULIST_RE else "ol"
            blocks.append(_render_list(tag, items))
            continue
        # Paragraph: run to the next blank line or other block starter.
        paragraph = [line]
        i += 1
        while i < n and not _starts_new_block(lines[i]):
            paragraph.append(lines[i])
            i += 1
        blocks.append(_render_paragraph(paragraph))
    return "\n".join(blocks)

Nothing inside code spans becomes a link. 2. A command line: `python -m mdlite FILE` prints the HTML for FILE followed by a newline; without FILE it reads standard input. 3. A user reports that `# a < b` produced a heading with a raw `<` in it. Make sure headings, list items and paragraphs are all escaped, and add a test. When you're done, give me a short summary of the module's structure and of anything in the spec you found ambiguous. "

"""Command-line interface: ``python -m mdlite [FILE]``.

With FILE, converts that file; without an argument, converts standard
input. The HTML is printed followed by a single newline.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import sys

from mdlite import to_html


def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> None:
    """Convert FILE (or stdin when FILE is omitted) and print the HTML."""
    argv = sys.argv[1:] if argv is None else argv
    if argv:
        try:
            with open(argv[0], encoding="utf-8") as handle:
                text = handle.read()
        except OSError as exc:
            print(f"mdlite: {exc}", file=sys.stderr)
            raise SystemExit(1)
    else:
        text = sys.stdin.read()
    sys.stdout.write(to_html(text) + "\n")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

"""Tests for the command line: python -m mdlite [FILE]."""

import subprocess
import sys
from pathlib import Path

from mdlite import to_html

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent


def _run_cli(args: list[str], stdin: str | None = None) -> subprocess.CompletedProcess:
    return subprocess.run(
        [sys.executable, "-m", "mdlite", *args],
        input=stdin,
        capture_output=True,
        text=True,
        cwd=ROOT,
    )


def test_file_argument(tmp_path):
    text = "# Title\n\n**bold**\n"
    path = tmp_path / "doc.md"
    path.write_text(text, encoding="utf-8")
    result = _run_cli([str(path)])
    assert result.returncode == 0
    assert result.stdout == to_html(text) + "\n"


def test_reads_stdin_without_file():
    text = "a < b and **c**"
    result = _run_cli([], stdin=text)
    assert result.returncode == 0
    assert result.stdout == to_html(text) + "\n"


def test_empty_input_prints_only_newline():
    result = _run_cli([], stdin="")
    assert result.returncode == 0
    assert result.stdout == "\n"


def test_missing_file_fails():
    result = _run_cli([str(Path(__file__).parent / "no_such_file.md")])
    assert result.returncode == 1
    assert "no_such_file.md" in result.stderr
